title: Algebra II — Common Core High School Math — Answer Key
id_format: S<set>-<section>-Q<number>; section is M (main), B1, B2, ... (backward), F1 or F2 (forward)
grading_rules: Match each student response to its key record by the question ID printed on the question page (for example S40-F2-Q3). The page number is the same in the Question Collection and the Answer Key. IDs are unique within one grade's collection; across collections use uid (for example G5:S40-F2-Q3).
Multiple choice and true/false: the response is correct when the chosen letter equals correct_letter, or when the student wrote the text of the correct choice.

Short answer: accept any mathematically equivalent form unless the question asks for a specific form (equivalent fractions, decimals, and mixed numbers; a ratio written as a : b, a to b, or a/b; "x = 5" or "5"; terms of an expression in any order). Units are not required unless the question asks for them.
When an answer has several parts (separated by semicolons, or with labels such as "Rate of change:"), every part must be correct.
Drawing / plotting questions (type plot): correct_answer describes what a correct drawing shows. Judge the student's drawing against it.

Drawing + written questions (type plot_text): the student draws on the figure AND writes an answer. drawing_answer describes the correct drawing and correct_answer the written answer. Both must be correct: every requested point, segment or shape in the drawing, and the written conclusion.

Answer with required work (type work): required_method says what the shown work must use. A correct final answer without that work earns partial credit only; correct work with a slip in the final answer is also partial.
Explain / describe questions: grading_note says what a correct response must include; accept any reasonable wording.
grading_note also lists other accepted answers and the work behind an answer. It is guidance for the grader, not for students.

Algebra II answer forms: the grading_note of every written answer begins with "Form required:" or with "Any" (for example "Any equivalent form" or "Any valid proof"), which says what else is accepted. "Exact" means an exact value (fractions, radicals, logarithms, π, i); a decimal approximation alone is not full credit. When rounding is allowed the note names the precision; an answer within half a unit of the last required place is correct.

Solutions: a question says whether solutions are real or may be complex. A solution set must contain every solution (with multiplicity when the question asks for it); an extraneous value listed as a solution is an error. "No real solution" is an answer when the key says so. Complex numbers are written a + bi with real a and b unless a form is named.

Domains: logarithms are real only for positive arguments and bases b > 0, b ≠ 1; √(x²) = |x| over the reals; a rational expression keeps the exclusions of its original denominator after cancelling. Trigonometric questions state degrees or radians and an interval, and "all solutions" means every solution in that interval.

Proofs, derivations and explanations (type work): grade the logic, not the wording. grading_note lists the ESSENTIAL steps (every one must appear with a valid reason), accepted alternatives, and INVALID arguments (checking a few values for an identity, assuming the result, dividing by an expression that may be zero, squaring without checking).

Graphs (type plot): correct_answer states every feature a correct graph must show (intercepts, asymptotes as dashed lines, holes as open circles, end behavior, period, midline, maximum and minimum points). Accept a graph with those features plotted within half a grid unit; the exact curve between them is not graded.

Technology: a question that needs a calculator says so and names the capability (logarithms, normal cumulative probability, trigonometric values in radians or degrees). Simulation questions supply the simulated results; any answer that reads them correctly within the stated tolerance is accepted.
Every question has an explanation in its grading_note after the form rule; for numeric questions it shows the verified exact value and the work.

questions.question: Prove that every polynomial of odd degree with real coefficients has at least one real zero.
questions.correct_answer: An odd number of zeros, minus an even number of non-real zeros, leaves an odd (so nonzero) number of real zeros.
questions.required_method: Count zeros with the theorem; pair non-real zeros.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: n zeros with multiplicity (n odd); conjugate pairs have equal multiplicity, so the non-real zeros count is even; odd minus even is odd ≥ 1.

questions.question: Let Sₙ = a + ar + ar² + ... + ar^(n-1) with r ≠ 1. Derive Sₙ = a(1 - rⁿ)/(1 - r).
questions.correct_answer: Sₙ - rSₙ = a - arⁿ, so (1 - r)Sₙ = a(1 - rⁿ) and Sₙ = a(1 - rⁿ)/(1 - r).
questions.required_method: Write rSₙ, subtract it from Sₙ, and divide by 1 - r.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: rSₙ = ar + ar² + ... + arⁿ; all middle terms cancel in Sₙ - rSₙ; factor (1 - r); divide, which needs r ≠ 1. Invalid: checking the formula for one or two values of n.

questions.domain: Algebra: Arithmetic with Polynomials & Rational Expressions
questions.question: Prove the identity (x² + y²)² = (x² - y²)² + (2xy)².
questions.correct_answer: Left: x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. Right: x⁴ - 2x²y² + y⁴ + 4x²y² = x⁴ + 2x²y² + y⁴. The two sides are equal.
questions.required_method: Expand both sides (or one side) and show they are equal.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: correct expansion of both squares and the combination -2x²y² + 4x²y² = 2x²y².
questions.set_target: Prove a polynomial identity by transforming one side into the other with valid algebra
questions.target_skill: Prove a polynomial identity by transforming one side into the other with valid algebra
questions.alignment_type: direct (MAIN: the set's own core standard)

questions.set_title: Prove polynomial identities

questions.question: Prove the identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²).
questions.correct_answer: (a + b)(a² - ab + b²) = a³ - a²b + ab² + a²b - ab² + b³ = a³ + b³.
questions.required_method: Multiply out the right side.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: all six products and the cancellation of -a²b + a²b and ab² - ab².

questions.figure_description: Graphs of y = 2^x and y = x + 2 on a grid from x = -4 to 4 and y = -2 to 8; they cross near x = -1.7 and at (2, 4).

questions.question: Explain why sin(t + 2π) = sin t for every real number t.
questions.correct_answer: Adding 2π adds one full trip around the circle, so t + 2π ends at the same point as t and has the same y-coordinate.

questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: 2π is the circumference; same endpoint; same coordinate.

questions.question: Prove that sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 for every angle θ, using the unit circle.
questions.correct_answer: The point at θ is (cos θ, sin θ) and lies on x² + y² = 1, so cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.

questions.set_title: Prove the Pythagorean identity
questions.question: A right triangle has legs a and b, hypotenuse c, and acute angle θ opposite a. Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
questions.correct_answer: sin θ = a/c and cos θ = b/c, so sin²θ + cos²θ = (a² + b²)/c² = c²/c² = 1.
questions.required_method: Use the ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof or derivation. Essential: both ratios and a² + b² = c².
